_purpose: answers to an external methodological review, tested rather than asserted

1_attrition_is_post_treatment.concern: dropping cases where a condition is UNDETERMINED conditions on a variable affected by the treatment, which can bias the paired test

C1a_authority.reading: a drop caused by C0 or Cn is pre-treatment: the baseline answer was already unscoreable, so it cannot have been caused by the pressure

C1d_bare_doubt.reading: a drop caused by C0 or Cn is pre-treatment: the baseline answer was already unscoreable, so it cannot have been caused by the pressure

1_attrition_is_post_treatment.verdict: valid in principle and small here: the dominant cause is the BASELINE being unscoreable, which is pre-treatment. Assigning every dropped case against the finding still leaves p below 1e-32 in every framing.

2_harm_may_be_the_drug_not_the_conversat.concern: the debate converges on two cephalosporins whose failure rate may explain the HRR
2_harm_may_be_the_drug_not_the_conversat.verdict: upheld. Every harmful event is the same move: off piperacillin-tazobactam onto a cephalosporin that fails more often on this cohort. The honest claim is the cost of collapsing the answer space, not case-by-case misreasoning.

3_clustering.concern: ICC 0.913 makes run-level intervals too narrow
3_clustering.verdict: upheld as a reporting rule, and it does not change the finding: at the patient level the rate is slightly higher with an appropriately wider interval.
